content: 1. Efavirenz metabolism is influenced by the hepatic enzyme CYP2B6. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of efavirenz by inducing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 2. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels and therapeutic effect of elacestrant by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered, and close monitoring is required. 3. Rifampin increases the metabolism of elafibranor, leading to reduced plasma levels and efficacy. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 4. Elagolix increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Conversely, rifampin increases elagolix levels through other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Rifampin also decreases elagolix levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Concomitant use of elagolix 150 mg daily with rifampin should be limited to six months. 5. Rifampin significantly reduces the plasma levels and therapeutic effect of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of reduced efficacy. 6. Rifampin decreases the plasma levels and efficacy of eletriptan by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered, and close monitoring is required. 7. Eliglustat increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Rifampin reduces eliglustat levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Strong CYP3A inducers significantly decrease eliglustat exposure, and coadministration is not recommended. 8. Rifampin reduces eltrombopag levels by inducing CYP1A2 and CYP2C9/10-mediated metabolism. Eltrombopag increases rifampin levels by decreasing its metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 9. Rifampin increases eluxadoline levels by decreasing its metabolism. If coadministered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, the eluxadoline dose should be reduced to 75 mg twice daily. Alternative therapies should be considered. 10. Rifampin reduces elvitegravir levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A inducers may lead to decreased plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and associated protease inhibitors, resulting in therapeutic failure and potential resistance. This combination is contraindicated. 11. Rifampin reduces the plasma levels of enalapril by increasing its metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Enasidenib increases rifampin levels through other mechanisms. Coadministration with sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrates should be avoided due to the risk of serious toxicities. If unavoidable, substrate dosages should be adjusted, and close monitoring is required. 13. Encorafenib increases rifampin levels through other mechanisms. As an OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 inhibitor, encorafenib may increase the concentration and toxicity of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 substrates. Rifampin reduces encorafenib levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered, and close monitoring is required. 14. Rifampin reduces enfortumab vedotin levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 15. Rifampin reduces entrectinib levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 16. Rifampin reduces enzalutamide levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Consider using alternatives with minimal CYP3A4 induction potential. If unavoidable, increase the enzalutamide dose from 160 mg daily to 240 mg daily. If the CYP3A4 inducer is discontinued, revert to the original enzalutamide dose. Close monitoring is required. 17. Rifampin reduces eplerenone levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 18. Rifampin reduces erdafitinib levels by altering its metabolism. Erdafitinib increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If coadministration is unavoidable, separate administration by at least six hours before or after P-gp substrate administration. Alternative therapies should be considered. 19. Rifampin reduces ergotamine levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 20. Rifampin reduces erlotinib levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies should be considered. 21. Rifampin reduces erythromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 22. Rifampin reduces escitalopram levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 23. Rifampin reduces esomeprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 and CYP2C19-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 24. Rifampin reduces estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies should be considered. 25. Rifampin reduces estradiol vaginal levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 26. Rifampin reduces synthetic conjugated estrogens levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies should be considered. 27. Rifampin reduces esterified estrogens levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 28. Rifampin reduces estropipate levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative therapies should be considered. 29. Rifampin reduces eszopiclone levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Zopiclone AUC is reduced by 80% with rifampin coadministration, and a similar effect is expected with eszopiclone. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 30. Ethanol reduces rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents and is more likely with chronic ethanol use. The clinical significance is unknown. 31. Rifampin reduces ethinyl estradiol levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 32. Rifampin reduces ethosuximide levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 33. Rifampin reduces ethotoin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 34. Rifampin reduces etonogestrel levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 35. Rifampin reduces etoposide levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 36. Rifampin reduces etrasimod levels by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9-mediated metabolism. Rifampin is a strong CYP3A4 inducer and a moderate CYP2C8 and CYP2C9 inducer. Etrasimod systemic exposure is significantly reduced, and coadministration is contraindicated. 37. Rifampin reduces etravirine levels by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 38. Rifampin reduces eucalyptus levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 39. Rifampin reduces everolimus levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This combination is contraindicated. 40. Rifampin reduces exemestane levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. For patients receiving potent CYP3A4 inducers, the recommended exemestane dose is 50 mg daily after a meal. 41. Rifampin reduces fedratinib levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. The effect of coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers has not been studied. Alternative therapies should be considered. 42. Rifampin reduces felbamate levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 43. Rifampin reduces felodipine levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered. 44. Rifampin reduces fenfluramine levels through other mechanisms. Coadministration with drugs that increase serotonin may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 45. Rifampin reduces fentanyl levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers may lead to decreased fentanyl plasma concentrations, reduced efficacy, or withdrawal syndrome in dependent patients. After stopping a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 46. Rifampin reduces fesoterodine levels by inducing CYP3A4-mediated metabolism. Alternative therapies should be considered.
